proposal.hypothesis: All three balls are wider than the widest sphere grip these fingers can take (sphere=45 mm, V1 probe), and the widths are tennis_ball 66.5, racquetball 55.5 and apple 74.6 mm. At pad_angle_deg=25 the faces are only parallel at a moderate opening. At 55-75 mm they splay, so a jaw edge touches first (contact_types=edge,pinch) and squeezes the round object out of the jaws as the servo stalls. The 2 mm TPU skin on each pad also takes up opening width. If the moving pad is tilted to 40° the faces become parallel near a 60-75 mm opening. Thinning the TPU to 1 mm gives back about 2 mm of aperture and keeps the 0.9 friction.

may_regress: narrow grasp objects (<40 mm) whose faces will now be non-parallel when nearly closed

proposal.rationale: Evidence that the failure is geometric and not a matter of parameters. On every control the verdict is wrong_behavior with felt.stopped_by=slip. contact_types includes edge on all three, which is the splayed-face signature. peak_force is 52.67 / 43.84 / 44.59 N, far above the 15 N hard limit and the ball weights (41-68 g). That shows the jaws are squeezing a ball they cannot hold, not grasping weakly. The ball is ejected sideways, which loads the wrist: felt.stall_s is 2.28, 1.74 and 1.8 s, all on wrist_roll. felt.pad_drop_t is 4.0-4.76 s, so contact is lost during the lift and hold. travel_reached (0.68-1.07) is not a held lift, and payload_held_g is '-'. ik_residual_mm=0 and there are no joint_limit_hits, so reach is fine. I am changing only 2 fields, within max_edits 3. The relative changes are 0.6 and 0.5, within the limit of 1. groove_mm stays at 3 so the V-groove still centres the spheres. it006 and it002 regressed with similar ideas, so this change is more conservative: it keeps the groove and reduces the TPU skin rather than removing it.
ruled_out: rung0: every object is wider than the widest sphere grip (45 mm). Contact_types=edge and peak_force of 44-53 N, already past the 15 N limit, mean that no depth, close or speed range removes the face splay. S1 has already exhausted the grasp ranges (escalation_reason=s1_exhausted), and the similar reparams it003 and it005 gave delta mean 0

rung1: pick_up already runs the grasp primitive, the only one that provides lifts=grasp. Recomposing approach, grasp and release cannot change jaw geometry, and the failure is slip from edge contact, not a sequencing problem
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no library tool to use or adapt

rung3: no tool template gives a wider parallel pinch (the templates are stock, pad, hook, knob_cup, soft_tip, slot_inserter and probe). The objects accept only pinch, and a single-contact rack tool cannot provide pinch, so only the finger pads can fix the aperture and face angle
